Senior Clinical Research Associate (Sr CRA) / Senior Klinischer Monitor – Full-Time or Part-Time Available (m/w/d)

Job available in 12 locations: Stuttgart, Munich, Hamburg, Düsseldorf, Aachen, Leipzig, Berlin, Bonn, Frankfurt, Bremen, Remote, Ulm

Work Schedule
Standard (Mon-Fri)

Environmental Conditions
Office

Job Description

About Us

At Thermo Fisher Scientific, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Our Mission is to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. Through our PPD® clinical research services, we support clinical trials in more than 100 countries, delivering laboratory, digital and decentralized solutions that help bring life-changing therapies to patients faster.

Our global Clinical Operations teams provide end-to-end clinical trial support — from study start-up through close-out — across commercial and government-sponsored studies.

Why Join Thermo Fisher Scientific / PPD?

- Work on high-quality, global clinical trials across diverse therapeutic areas
- Be part of a stable, well-established organization with long-term career opportunities
- Strong collaboration with experienced CTMs and project teams
- Clear development pathways (e.g., Senior CRA, Lead CRA, CTM)
- Flexible working models that support work-life balance
- Permanent employment
- Full-time (40 hours/week) or Part-time (32 hours/week) options available

About the Role

This position is for experienced Clinical Research Associates with 2+ years of independent monitoring experience. You will manage clinical trial sites across Germany, ensuring studies are conducted in compliance with the protocol, ICH-GCP, applicable regulations, and company SOPs.

You’ll work autonomously, partner closely with investigative sites, and collaborate with project teams to deliver high-quality, inspection-ready clinical trials.

What You’ll Do

- Perform site monitoring activities (on-site and remote) using a risk-based monitoring approach
- Ensure protocol, ICH-GCP, regulatory, and SOP compliance at investigator sites
- Conduct SDR, SDV, CRF review, and investigational product accountability
- Identify, document, escalate, and follow up on issues through resolution, applying root cause analysis and CAPA principles
- Maintain audit and inspection readiness at all assigned sites
- Build strong, collaborative relationships with investigators and site staff
- Document monitoring activities in timely, high-quality reports and follow-up letters
- Maintain ongoing communication with sites between visits to support issue resolution and data quality
- Ensure study systems (e.g., CTMS) are updated according to study conventions
- Provide trial status updates and metrics to the Clinical Team Manager (CTM)
- Support study start-up, investigator identification, site initiation, and study close-out activities as assigned
- Participate in investigator meetings, audits, inspections, and project team meetings as required

Additional responsibilities may include supporting process improvement initiatives, mentoring activities, or project-specific tasks aligned with experience.

A Day in the Life

- Review site metrics and prioritize monitoring activities based on risk
- Conduct on-site or remote monitoring visits
- Partner with sites to resolve findings and improve processes
- Collaborate with CTMs and project teams to keep studies on track and inspection-ready
- Complete documentation, system updates, and administrative tasks

Education & Experience

- Bachelor’s degree in a life sciences related field or equivalent qualification
- Minimum 2+ years of experience as a Clinical Research Associate / Monitor
- Valid driver’s license
- Full right to work in Germany
- Fluency in German and English (C1 level) – interviews will be conducted in German

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

- Strong clinical monitoring skills with hands-on RBM experience
- Excellent understanding and application of ICH-GCP and applicable regulations
- Solid therapeutic area knowledge and medical terminology
- Well-developed critical thinking, problem-solving, and root cause analysis skills
- Strong written and verbal communication skills with medical professionals
- High attention to detail and strong organizational skills
- Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to cross-functional teams
- Flexibility and adaptability in a dynamic project environment
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and ability to learn clinical systems (e.g., CTMS)

Locations: Home-based or hybrid anywhere in Germany
FTE: Full-time (40 hrs/week) or Part-time 80% (32 hrs/week)
Contract: Permanent
Travel: Approximately 50–75% (study-dependent)

jobs.occupation: Biologe (m/w/d) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description:
About the LSM
The Graduate School Life Science Munich (LSM) is an international doctoral programme at one of Europe's leading research universities - Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München (LMU). The programme spans a wide range of disciplines including Biochemistry, Cell and Developmental Biology, Ecology, Genetics, Microbiology, Pharmacology, Plant Sciences, Zoology, and more. Doctoral candidates join a vibrant, diverse, and truly international research community at the LMU Biocenter in Planegg-Martinsried.

Doctoral Positions in Bioinformatics, Botany, Epigenetics, Ecology, Neuroscience, Plant Genetics, Systematic Zoology & more - Graduate School Life Science Munich (LSM), LMU Munich This year, two pathways are available:

1. Independent Research Proposals (new this year)
A number of LSM faculty members are open to receiving original research proposals in specific areas. Rather than applying to a pre-defined project, candidates develop their own original proposal inspired by the research interests of a participating faculty member. Should a proposal be of interest to the potential supervisor, they would be willing to support the candidate in identifying and applying for appropriate funding - such as a fellowship, scholarship, or third-party funding.
Participating faculty members and their research areas:

Prof. Claude Becker - Epigenetics, epigenomics, plant-microbe interactions, biosynthetic gene clusters

Prof. Alexander Keller - Biodiversity, AI and computer vision, plant-pollinator interactions, ecological genomics

Prof. Dario Leister - Regulation and improvement of photosynthesis (open to CSC candidates only)

Prof. Michael Matschiner - Phylogenetics, adaptive radiation, museum and fossil specimens

Dr. Natascha Turetzek - Arthropod evo-devo, gene duplication, sensory organ diversification, thermal stress

For full research area abstracts, please visit: https://www.bio.lmu.de/lsm/en/become-an-lsm-student/recruiting-labs-doctoral-positions/index.html#st_accordion__master_1

1. Doctoral Positions
The following doctoral positions are currently available. Please note that for all positions listed below, funding is still in the process of being secured.
Supervisors are committed to supporting promising candidates in identifying and applying for appropriate funding - such as a fellowship, scholarship, or third-party funding.

Antisense oligonucleotide treatment for MAST3-associated epilepsy - Prof. David Keays, Sensory and Developmental Neuroscience

Avian Cerebral Organoids - Prof. David Keays, Sensory and Developmental Neuroscience

Identification and Characterisation of Novel Microtubule Associated Proteins - Prof. David Keays, Sensory and Developmental Neuroscience

Transcriptional networks shaping the legume root symbiosis with nitrogen-fixing rhizobia - Prof. Martin Parniske, Plant Genetics

Harnessing natural genetic resources to defend fruits against insect attack - Prof. Martin Parniske, Plant Genetics

For full project descriptions, please visit: https://www.bio.lmu.de/lsm/en/become-an-lsm-student/recruiting-labs-doctoral-positions/index.html#st_accordion__master_2
Master's degree (MSc) or equivalent in biology, biochemistry, bioinformatics, biophysics, biotechnology, medicine, or a related discipline
In exceptional cases, a 4-year Bachelor's degree with Honours (min. 240 ECTS, with written thesis) is accepted
Proficiency in written and spoken English
The most recent final examination must have taken place no more than four years prior to the date of application
There are no tuition fees

An international, multidisciplinary doctoral programme at a world-class research institution
Individual mentoring and a structured Thesis Advisory Committee (TAC)
A wide range of transferable skills workshops, seminars, and career development opportunities
Financial support for conferences and scientific events
A vibrant student community at the LMU Biocenter

jobs.occupation: Testing Operator - Space Hardware Testing (all genders) (Werkstoffprüfer/in (mit Schwerpunkten))
jobs.description:
YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES THE WHY We build pressure vessels and carbon structures for spaceflight. Before our hardware flies, it gets tested — and you keep the testing running. Without you, the test bench stands still. THE WHAT You prepare tests, help run them, and document the results. You work in the lab and at the test bench — hands-on, in a team, with real space hardware every day. Your tasks in detail:
• Prepare and post-process the testing areas: You set up test benches and specimens, tear down after tests, and keep the testing area ready for action. → High Performance: The test bench is ready when the team needs it.
• Run and document tests: You support destructive testing and acceptance testing (NDT) and record every step cleanly. → Accountability: What was tested is documented. No gaps.
• Say what you see: Anything unusual about a specimen, the test bench, or a result — you report it right away, not when someone asks. → Candor: You raise problems before they grow.
• Support the team and infrastructure: You pitch in where needed — in the testing team and with technical infrastructure on site. → Togetherness: We win as a team.
• Learn new things: NDT methods, new test procedures, new materials — you want to grow. We'll train you. → Playfulness: Curiosity is a strength here, not a distraction.

YOUR PROFILE
• Training: Completed vocational training as a materials tester / Werkstoffprüfer (plastics, metals, or fiber composites/CFRP) or comparable technical training.
• Experience: First experience in a test lab or materials testing is a plus — not a must. What matters more: you want to learn.
• Work style: Motivated, reliable, hands-on. You want the job done — and done right.
• Team player: You enjoy working with others and help out when things get busy.
• Languages: German and English, each at B2 minimum — one of the two confident for daily work.
• On-site: This role is 100% on-site in Taufkirchen. The lab and test bench don't fit in a home office.

#LI-Onsite

WHAT WE OFFER
• Creative freedom & responsibility: Autonomy, scope for decision-making and short implementation paths.
• Flexible working hours & remote option: You can work remotely by arrangement.
• Culinary variety: Lunch together with fresh, varied dishes every day.
• Attractive additional benefits: Choose between Deutschlandticket, EGYM-Well pass or a monthly top-up payment card (GivveCard).
• Knowledge exchange at the highest level: Work with experienced engineers and experts from the aerospace industry.
• Dynamic environment: Exciting projects, development opportunities and a start-up atmosphere with agile, cross-functional collaboration.
• Community & team spirit: Monthly blackout events for socialising, networking and exchange.
• Unique working atmosphere : Enjoy the end of the working day on our large roof terrace with a view of the Alps!

About us Blackwave designs, manufactures and ships flight-qualified, commercial off-the-shelf composite overwrapped pressure vessels (COPVs) for launch vehicles and satellites. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Munich, Germany, the company delivers COPVs from a standardized portfolio with flight heritage. The approach reduces lead time from months to days while ensuring that each tank is qualified and flight-ready. Blackwave's mission is to end COPV failure in spaceflight. The company employs more than 150 people across manufacturing facilities in Germany and Texas.More information at Blackwave.com and the procurement platform COPV.com.

jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLEERC is bringing Victor, our hybrid-electric heavy-lift cargo UAS, to military operators and customers to enable critical missions when roads, runways, or crewed aviation are unavailable, impractical, or operationally constrained. In this role, you will drive the introduction of this new capability based on a clear view of customer missions, capability needs, procurement pathways, and operational constraints.
You will build and own ERC's relationships with the Armed Forces of Germany, NATO partners, and global allies. Combining strategic market development, hands-on key account ownership, and capture execution, you will turn operational needs into qualified opportunities, test and evaluation projects, and contracts. In pursuing your mission, you will be working closely with our Commercial Leadership as well as Product, Engineering, Flight Operations, and Communications.
WHAT YOU WILL DO
• Develop account and market-entry plans for Germany and selected NATO/allied markets
• Build, maintain, and expand durable relationships with military users, capability planners, procurement stakeholders, prime contractors, and operational units
• Identify and qualify defence opportunities ahead of formal tenders; maintain account plans, develop opportunity-specific capture plans, and set pipeline priorities
• Drive opportunities from initial engagement to contract signature, including customer briefings, requirement shaping, proposal development, offer coordination, negotiations, and follow-up
• Navigate military procurement processes and coordinate complex stakeholder landscapes across end users, requirements owners, procurement bodies, industry partners, and internal teams
• Work closely with Product, Engineering, Flight Operations, and Leadership to translate operational needs into mission concepts, demonstration narratives, product requirements, and commercially viable solutions
• Support the planning and execution of product demonstrations, trade fairs, and industry events; and represent ERC at customer meetings, delegation visits, demonstrations, field exercises, trade fairs, and defence events.

WHAT YOU BRING
• Approximately 5 years of experience in business development, key account management, or sales, ideally in the defence or governmental sector or in complex B2B enterprise sales
• A proven record of developing and closing complex opportunities with military, governmental, defence-industry, or enterprise customers
• Strong commercial judgement and the ability to combine account strategy with hands-on project execution
• Excellent communication, stakeholder-management, and negotiation skills, including with senior military, governmental, and industrial counterparts in English and German
• A strong understanding of the German defence ecosystem and acquisition pathways
• A structured and ownership-oriented working style
• Authorization to work in Germany, the eligibility to obtain the appropriate security clearances as may be required; and willingness to travel.

Moreover, it would be helpful if you also
• bring an active network among military users, requirements owners, and procurement stakeholders
• are familiar with military procurement processes of NATO and allied countries.

ERC particularly encourages veterans and former military service members to apply for this position.

WHAT WE OFFER
• Full-scale aerospace engineering, not concept slides
• A 60+ engineer team at Ottobrunn
• Real ownership and flat hierarchies: a modern startup culture where your input shapes decisions, not just execution
• Flexible working hours, remote work, and competitive compensation
• Health & wellbeing: EGYM Wellpass membership and subsidized lunch in our canteen
• Office extras: espresso coffee, fresh fruit, and soft drinks, plus regular team and company events, and plenty more once you're on board

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

jobs.occupation: Working student (d/f/m) in the area of Flight Dynamics (Ingenieur/in - Luft- und Raumfahrttechnik)
jobs.description:
About us

Airbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. The Company constantly innovates to provide efficient and technologically-advanced solutions in aerospace, defence, and connected services. In commercial aircraft, Airbus offers modern and fuel-efficient airliners and associated services. Airbus is also a European leader in defence and security and one of the world's leading space businesses. In helicopters, Airbus provides the most efficient civil and military rotorcraft solutions and services worldwide.
Job description

In order to support the Flight Dynamics department, Airbus Defence and Space is looking for a

Working student (d/f/m) in the area of Flight Dynamics

You are a full time student (d/f/m), looking for a working student position and want to get to know the work of a Flight Dynamics Engineer (d/f/m)?  Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the Flight Dynamics department as a working student (d/f/m) with approx. 18 hours a week!

- Location: Manching
- Start: Dezember 2026
- Duration: 12 months

The Flight Dynamics team in Manching develops in-house advanced software tools aimed at large data analysis and post processing. In this context, verification and validation of these tools is required to ensure compliance to the specific tools process.

Definition working student

Working students are students who are enrolled at a University or some other institution of higher education, and who are employed in a reasonably long, fixed-term position parallel to their studies. This position must not be confused with an internship or with the possibility of writing a final thesis.

This employment usually takes place directly on the company's premises. A working student's main focus remains on their studies, which is why, during term-time, working students are not allowed to work more than 20 hours per week.

Working students therefore usually work near their place of study, so as to conveniently combine studying and employment.

Your location

Located about an hour’s drive north of Munich, Manching is an up-and-coming market town that offers a wide range of leisure and cultural activities. Here, you can enjoy the quality of life in the countryside while the pleasures of near-by cities are still within easy reach.

Your benefits

- Attractive salary and work-life balance with an 18-hour week (flexitime).
- A final thesis is possible after consultation with the department.
- Mobile working after agreement with the department.
- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.
- Work with modern/diversified technologies.
- At Airbus, we see you as a valuable team member and you are not hired to brew coffee, instead you are in close contact with the interfaces and are part of our weekly team meetings.
- Opportunity to participate in the Generation Airbus Community to expand your own network.

Your tasks and responsibilities

- Checking the scope and code of the tool and the already existing tests as a baseline for discussion and required depth of test coverage.
- Checking the requirements defined as Jira tickets of the tool and discuss potential unclear formulations as well as the scope of testing.
- Choosing requirements to test within a one-week time horizon.
- Implementing test cases within the defined scope (i.e., automatized, repeated, checking edge conditions, checking correct and incorrect user handling,...).
- Incorporating the test cases in the continuous integration pipeline, executing it, and checking the results.
- Documenting the outcome of the tests (i.e., results, limitation, bugs, potential improvements) within the tool’s documentation and reviewing the implemented test cases, discussion of improvements, and providing deliverables on a weekly basis.

Desired skills and qualifications

- Enrolled full time student (d/f/m) within computer science, data science, informatics or related disciplines.
- Extensive experience in at least one of the following programming languages:
- Java 1.8 and JUnit4 or JUnit5
- Matlab R2024b and testsuite
- Python 3.12 and pytest
- Extensive experience in continuous integration pipeline setup in Jenkins.
- Extensive experience in working with git, specifically Bitbucket as well as knowledge in working with Atlassian toolset, like Confluence and Jira.
- Knowledge of SLURM workload manager
- Knowledge of Linux, Microsoft Word and Latex to report results.
- Understanding of Flight Dynamics (e.g., nonlinear simulation) is a plus.
- Understanding of database structures (e.g., sqlite) and large data storages (e.g., HDF5 or parquet) is a plus.
- Self-organized, team-oriented way of working.
- Advanced English, German is a plus.

Please upload the following documents: cover letter, CV, relevant transcripts, enrollment certificate.

Not a 100% match? No worries! Airbus supports your personal growth.

Take your career to a new level and apply online (https://www.airbus.com/en/careers) now!

jobs.occupation: Technical Program Manager (f/m/d) (Ingenieur/in - Maschinenbau)
jobs.employer_name: Siemens Energy Global GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description:
A Snapshot of Your Day 

As a Junior Technology Analyst (f/m/d), you will support the Technology Manager by gathering, structuring, and maintaining technology scouting intelligence across emerging technologies, startups, research developments, market signals, and innovation ecosystems relevant to Grid Technologies. Your typical day will involve monitoring technology domains, conducting desk research, and preparing technology opportunity profiles. You will play a key role in ensuring that external signals are captured consistently and translated into clear inputs for further assessment, contributing to the PRM Technology Radar and other analytical activities.

How You’ll Make an Impact 

* Monitor selected technology domains, startups, research institutions, publications, and market developments relevant to Grid Technologies
* Capture early technology signals and maintain structured scouting inputs across H1–H4 horizons
* Maintain and update Technology Radar entries, ensuring consistent documentation of technology signals and assessment status
* Support preparation for interactions with startups, universities, and research institutes, including background notes and technology summaries
* Maintain scouting records and briefing materials in the central repository, preparing concise summaries and visual inputs for technology briefings
* Use digital and AI-enabled tools to improve searchability, synthesis, and reuse of technology intelligence

What You Bring

* Relevant bachelor’s degree or diploma in engineering, technology management, business, innovation management, data analytics, or a related field
* First expereinces in technology scouting, research, strategy, innovation, R&D, consulting, or market intelligence
* Very good understanding of research and the technology of Siemens Energy, with a willingness to learn more
* Curiosity for emerging technologies, energy systems, grid technologies, startups, and innovation ecosystems
* Strong analytical skills with the ability to structure information and summarize complex topics clearly
* Fluent in English, with good communication skills and attention to detail
